findings.title: Embedded-post username color changed on light themes
findings.body: The light-theme branch of `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was rewritten from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, and the dark branch uses 30% instead of the complement 70%. Light-theme embedded-post usernames become much lighter than before, and dark themes get the old light-theme shade rather than a readable secondary-based color.

findings.title: Group member name lightness not preserved
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses 50% for both `dark-light-choose` arguments. Light themes lose the darker 30% treatment (the sibling `.title` was already 50%), and dark themes do not get the complementary 70% on `$secondary`.

findings.title: Mobile group member name lightness not preserved
findings.body: Same mistake as desktop: `.group-member-info .name` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(..., 50%, ..., 50%)`. Light-theme names are lighter than before, and the dark-theme color is not the 70% complement of the original 30%.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness does not match desktop
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and should map to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, which is what desktop/topic-post.scss does. Mobile now uses 50%/50%, so light-theme map headings are much lighter and dark themes do not get the intended secondary shade.

findings.title: Custom message length color arguments are inverted
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new call is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light branch is no longer 70%, so light themes get a darker hint, and the dark branch keeps 70% on `$secondary` instead of the complementary 30% used everywhere else for a 70% primary scale.

findings.title: Category badge notification still scales only $primary
findings.body: In the same file this PR updates, `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still sets `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. On dark themes that stays a lightened primary and will not follow the secondary-based color the neighboring topic-list text now uses.
